text.p: Copper hit a new year high for the second day running on continued tight supply.

Copper ended in the plus column above the psychological $2,500 level on Wednesday, although early momentum dwindled after prices touched new one-year highs. Three months metal finished the PM kerb $13 stronger at $2,506 per tonnes after stalling at a high of $2,518.

In tandem, the cash to threes backwardation also flared out to around $85/$90 at one point, from around $70 at the end of business on Tuesday. Cash/threes then contracted slightly to $81/$85 by the end of the kerb.
Other base metals, most of which had climbed higher with copper in the morning and earlier this week, ended up with pared gains after initially trying the upside.
Aluminium was barely firmer at $1,652, up just $5.
Lead, which leaped to $648 in a speculative, copper-led rally earlier in the day, followed suit and slid off its highs by the end of the kerb. But it was still a solid $14 higher at $637.
Nickel tumbled sharply by $130 to $7,560, filling a chart gap between $7,620 and $7,660 which was left when prices initially rallied above $2,500 two weeks ago.
The other metals were unremarkable, with tin ending the day at a $35 lower $5,755. Alloy was down $17 at $1,500.

New York precious metals ended weaker Wednesday in generally quiet dealings in contrast to the sharp moves earlier in the week. COMEX June gold settled 30 cents firmer at $343.70 an ounce, traded $344.00 to $342.20. Bullion was quoted late afternoon by dealers at $342.70/$343.20 an ounce from $342.25 in London. Fundamentally gold looked sound according to producer body World Gold Council whose report issued Wednesday noted that consumption in key world markets shot up 17 percent to a record 771 tonnes in the first quarter of the year.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed mostly firmer as the market attempted to consolidate following a steep slide Tuesday to a six-week low in the new crop July contract, traders said. The market found support on news Egypt overnight bought 400,000 tonnes of U.S. soft red winter wheat and may be seeking more. CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed 1-3/4 cents per bushel higher to 1-1/2 lower, with July up 1-3/4 at $3.82-1/4.

NYMEX crude oil futures and unleaded gasoline rallied at the close of trading to settle broadly higher Wednesday on late reports that Turkish forces had staged another incursion across the border of Iraq. Heating oil, taking a back seat to the rest of the action, ended mostly firmer, with only the nearby June contract settling lower. July crude oil rose 27 cents, settling at $21.86 a barrel on its first session as the spot month, after trading in a $21.95-$21.46 range. Nearby August settled one cent higher, at $21.87 a barrel.
